title: queue ticket
description: One change waiting its turn in the queue of a served thing, a file in <served folder>/<app folder>/.queue/, so every writer of it (CLI runs, servers, UI clicks) stands in one line and changes go one at a time (ADR-S14). A ticket, never a command: each process runs its own change, and nothing in a served folder is ever executed. Two app versions share the queue at once: apiVersion, kind and metadata never change; spec may grow (ADR-S15). How every app shares the folder is fixed for v1 in the README, section The change queue on disk.

apiVersion.description: The form the ticket is in, the same as the backend marker. It never changes, so two app versions sharing the queue both read every ticket (ADR-S15).

kind.description: Always QueueTicket. It tells a ticket apart from the backend marker, which carries the same apiVersion.

metadata.description: Who waits and where in the line. It never changes in v1, since every app reads every other's tickets by it (ADR-S15).

id.description: The ticket's place in the line and its file name without .json: 20 digits, so their order as strings is their order as numbers, and a lower id goes first.

app.description: The product ID of the app that waits, so a person reading the queue sees which app holds each place.

pid.description: The process that waits, on host, so a person can find the process behind a ticket.

host.description: The machine the process runs on, as it names itself. A pid means something only on its own machine, so host says which one.

change.description: What the change does, for people reading the queue.

joinedAt.description: When the ticket joined the line, as an RFC 3339 time, so a person reading the queue sees how long a change has waited.

version.description: The version of the app that waits. Two app versions may share one queue, so a person sees which one holds each place.

spec.description: What the ticket says about its change. Open: a newer app may add fields here, and an older reader accepts them (CT-RULE-4).
